- [x] Hands-free phone updates (Meka approved 2026-10-07 23:09): after every green CI run on main that touched `android/` or `core/`, GitHub builds the debug APK and publishes it, so the Fold offers "MEKA update ready" with no Mac involved. **Signing:** the Mac's debug keystore is in the GitHub Actions secret `MEKA_FOLD_SIGNING_KEY` (base64; Meka adds it with "Copy phone signing key.command"; password/alias are the debug defaults `android`/`androiddebugkey`); the workflow decodes it to a temp file, signs, and deletes it; never echoed or uploaded as an artifact. If the secret is missing the job skips with a notice (not a failure). versionCode stays the commit count, so CI and Mac builds never clash (same commit = same build; the server already refuses a build that isn't newer). **Publishing identity (security):** a dedicated release-only publisher — not a household device: a P-256 key whose private half lives in Secrets Manager `meka-os-dev/release-publisher`, readable only by the GitHub OIDC deploy role; its public key registered on the server as kind `release_publisher` for Meka's household, which may call only `/v1/releases/upload` and `/v1/releases/chunk` (every other route 403; unit-test that), and is listed in Activity as "GitHub build". The phone still checks the SHA-256 and Android still refuses anything not signed with the installed key; nothing installs without Meka's tap. Add a quiet "MEKA update ready" notification (low-importance channel, at most once per build) so he knows without opening the app. Keep `publish-fold.sh` working as the manual fallback. Infra test for the secret and role grant; backend tests for the publisher scope. Then tell Meka in the run summary that phone updates arrive on their own.
  - *Slice 1, 2026-10-07 (core touched, so Mac checked nightly):* the pipeline. **Infra:** Secrets Manager `meka-os-dev/release-publisher` (the P-256 private key; a resource-policy Deny on GetSecretValue for every principal except `role/meka-os-github-deploy`, the service included) and `meka-os-dev/release-publisher-public` (`{"public_key": …}`, read by the service; env `MEKA_RELEASE_PUBLISHER_SECRET`), both `{}` until the workflow makes the pair (about $0.80/month together); infra test for the deny, no grant of the private key and the service's read. **Server:** `ReleasePublisher` (backend/ReleasePublisher.kt): not a household device and no bearer secret — `Authorization: Publisher github-build` plus the usual request signature, checked against the public key (re-read each minute); it publishes for the server's one household (refused if there are none or several) and may call only `/v1/releases/latest` (to see what is already published, which the plan's "chunk" became: downloading builds isn't the publisher's business) and `/v1/releases/upload`; every other route answers 403, no device can be called `github-build` (device ids are `[a-z0-9]`), and its builds are stored as published by `github-build`. Backend tests (ReleasePublisherTest: publish → the Fold fetches it, same build again, not newer, every other route 403 incl. chunk, another key / replay / wrong name / wrong route, no key set, two households). The same file has the publisher's client and commands (`backend publisher-keygen | publisher-latest | publisher-publish`, no database; the private key only from the environment). **Workflow:** a `publish-fold` job in deploy.yml after the server deploy (or its skip): skips with a notice when `MEKA_FOLD_SIGNING_KEY` isn't set; makes the publisher's key pair the first time (public half first); asks the server for the published build and skips with a notice unless `android/`, `core/`, `design/` or the build files changed since the commit that build was made from (main is linear: build N is the Nth commit); decodes the keystore into the runner's debug-key place, checks it opens with the debug defaults, builds `assembleDebug` (full history, so versionCode is the commit count), checks with apksigner that the APK carries that very certificate, publishes, and always deletes both keys from the runner. "Not newer" (e.g. the Mac published this commit first) is a notice, not a failure. **Fold:** a quiet "MEKA update ready" notification (`app_update` channel, low importance, "Build 412 · 24.3 MB · open MEKA to install") once per build and only while MEKA isn't on screen; Later or nothing on offer withdraws it; `AppUpdateRules.shouldNotify/told/notificationLine`, unit-tested. **Mac:** `tools/Copy phone signing key.command` copies its debug key as base64 and opens the repo's new-secret page (Needs Meka #14). `publish-fold.sh` is unchanged as the manual fallback.
  - *Live 2026-10-07:* CI green (run 37697302079); deploy run 37697539793 deployed the server, made the publisher's key pair and **published the first phone build from GitHub** (the signing secret was already set, and the APK's certificate matched the Mac's debug key).
  - *Slice 2, 2026-10-07 (core touched, so Mac checked nightly):* the GitHub build in Activity. When a build from the release-only publisher is complete, the server (`ReleaseActivity`, backend/ReleasePublisher.kt, through `Releases`' new `onPublished`) writes one `agent_action` entry of the new kind `PUBLISHED` into Meka's synced data as server-authored ops (ADR-008 addendum; fixed op ids, so once per build) and wakes the devices: "GitHub build published build 412" · "MEKA 0.1.412 · 24.3 MB · install it from Today on the Fold" · "Why: Hands-free phone updates · after a green CI run on main", nothing to undo, and the week line counts "1 phone build". Both apps' Activity panes show it as they show every entry (no app change); builds the Mac publishes by hand aren't listed. Core `ActivityRules.releaseId/releaseSummary/releaseFields`; entries of a kind an app doesn't know are skipped. Tests: ActivityTest (both devices, unknown kind), backend ReleaseActivityTest (listed once, re-publish writes nothing, next build a second entry, a Mac build or an incomplete one isn't listed, wake once). CI green (run 37699788994; macOS job at the next nightly run; the server redeploys).

Decided: a luxury-watch feel, built around the **Day ring**, gold on black; one ambient element, never several competing.
  1. **The Day ring is always on Today** (not only as an opening moment, and still after Shut down — then it shows tomorrow's first commitment): pinned under the greeting at a comfortable size (≈ 180 dp closed Fold, larger unfolded; Mac at the top of Today).

  3. **Breathing glow**: the ring's brass edge brightens and dims slowly (≈ 5 s cycle, 60 %→100 %), like a sleeping laptop light — calm, not flashing. At the top of each hour a single gentle shimmer runs round the ring.

  1. **Side button = "open MEKA already listening"** (default digital assistant role, `ROLE_ASSISTANT` / `VoiceInteractionService` or the assist intent): long-press the side key → MEKA's Talk panel opens listening. The setup screen walks Meka through Settings → Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant app → MEKA (Samsung: Side key → Press and hold → Wake Bixby→ change to "Digital assistant").
  2. **Auto-listen where it's clearly wanted:** when MEKA opens with **Bluetooth headphones or a car** connected, from the **home-screen Talk widget**, from the bedside clock (half folded), or from the cover screen's mic.
  3. **"Listen when I open MEKA" — a setting, off by default** (Ask → More → Talk). When on: the orb appears and listens for up to 6 s after Today opens; stops on silence; **skips when it's noisy** (measures the room for 300 ms first; above ~60 dBA it shows "Too noisy — tap to talk" instead); never when opened from a notification; a quiet chime marks listening.
  4. **Safety unchanged:** nothing destructive or sent without a spoken/tapped yes; every change has Undo; other people's speech reads as Meka's, so the confirmation is the real guard — speaker recognition is not built now (no reliable public on-device speaker-ID API, poor in noise; revisit in V2 as an optional extra check).
  5. **"Hey MEKA" wake word** stays a later option (battery, false triggers).

Shared-element transitions (Plan → Today, list → detail) moved to the App shell item, where navigation lands.*

- [x] Repeating tasks and routines (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly; "every 2nd Tuesday"; skip/snooze one occurrence)
  - *2026-10-06 (Mac checked nightly):* core `Recurrence` (RRULE subset: every N days, weekly on chosen days incl. every other week, monthly on a date — the 31st falls on a short month's last day — or on the 1st–4th/last weekday, yearly incl. 29 Feb), `CivilDate` and a platform `LocalCalendar` so times of day survive the clock change; unit-tested. A repeating task is a series of occurrences: Done or Skip creates the next one with an id made from the series and day, so two devices finishing the same one offline end up with one next occurrence; missed ones aren't back-filled (an open one from an earlier day stays, marked "since Mon 5 Oct"). "Tomorrow" snoozes just this occurrence (or any one-off task) out of Today and the planner until its day. Steps on a repeating task make it a routine: each new occurrence brings them back unticked. Fold: Repeat row in the task detail unfolds the picker (Every day · Every weekday · Every Tue · Every 2 weeks on Tue · Monthly on the 6th · Monthly on the 1st Tue · Every year on 6 Oct), steps with spring ticks, and Done · Skip · Tomorrow · Delete; rows show "↻ Every weekday". Mac: the same as a Repeat menu, steps list and buttons.

- [x] Lists: Waiting for (with chase dates), Someday (with kinds), Decisions (with review dates)
  - *2026-10-06 (Mac checked nightly):* core `Lists` (non-AI). Waiting for is a `commitment` owed to you: what, from whom, a chase date (presets Tomorrow · In 3 days · Next week · In 2 weeks · No date; default 3 days); "Chased" records it and sets the next chase 3 days on; "Got it" closes it (Done wins over a chase made at the same time on the other device). Someday is a task with lifecycle SOMEDAY grouped by kind (Ideas · To buy · Projects · Trips · To read · To look into · Applications · Home · Other), never in Today or the planner; "Do it now" puts it back in Today, and a one-off task's detail has "Someday" to send it there (repeating tasks can't). Decisions: what you decided, why, an optional review date (a month · 3 months · 6 months · a year); when due: "Still right" with the next review, Revisit, or Replace (the old one is kept as superseded, so it isn't re-made). Chase and review dates are days (stored as 09:00 local). Due chases and reviews show as one "From your lists" card in Needs you and count in its badge. Unit-tested incl. two-device sync. Fold: Lists tab with a springing tab pill, rows that unfold their actions, date chips and add fields. Mac: the same with a segmented control and menus.

Server sends through FCM HTTP v1 with the service account in Secrets Manager `meka-os-dev/fcm/service-account` (service account pasted by Meka 2026-10-07; empty `{}` = push off, keep local notifications as the fallback).

Server: `Push` + `FcmSender` (backend/Push.kt, Fcm.kt): when a device stores ops, the household's other devices are sent one data-only FCM message `{"t":"sync"}` (normal priority, collapse key `sync`, TTL 1 h; nothing about Meka's data goes to Google), at most one every 20 s per device with one trailing wake at the end of the gap; sent off the request. The service account is read from Secrets Manager at use time (5-min cache, `{}` = off, refused unless it's a `service_account` for Google's own token endpoint); the RS256 JWT-bearer assertion is signed with the JDK, the access token cached; a token FCM calls unregistered is forgotten. `POST /v1/push/token` (signed, keyed devices only; empty token removes it) into `push_token` (V6 migration, additive; revoked devices never woken). Wire: `WireCodec.PushToken` (shape-checked). Core: `PushApi` on the HTTP transport, `MekaCore.registerPushToken` (false = try later, e.g. a server without push). Unit-tested: wire, transport, the coalescing, gone tokens, other households, the JWT (verified against the key), the FCM request and token reuse, the Postgres store. Fold: Firebase Messaging 24.1.0 (FCM only, no Analytics; analytics/ad-id collection meta-data off), configured from `res/values/firebase.xml` (the google-services plugin's values, checked against google-services.json by `PushTest`, no extra Gradle plugin); `push/MekaMessagingService` runs `SyncWorker.syncSoon` (expedited one-off, network-constrained) on a wake, so Today, the widgets, ongoing notifications and the governor follow a Mac edit within seconds; the token is sent once per new token (on start, after connecting, and retried at each background sync until the server has it); nothing is shown for a wake. When the fixtures feed moves a timed match whose old kick-off was still ahead, the server writes `movedFromMs`/`movedAtMs` on it (additive, fixtures only; ADR-008 addendum). Core: `FixtureMoves` (pure) and a new governor source, **Kick-off changes** (Heads-up, can be lowered to Digest or App only; listed in Notifications on both apps): "Kick-off moved: Barça v Real Madrid" · "Now 21:00 · was 18:30 · Sat 10 Oct" ("Now Sun 11 Oct 18:30 · was Sat 10 Oct 21:00" when the day changed), once per new time, stale after two days or at kick-off; hidden fixtures stay quiet; tapping opens Today. - [x] Search everything (tasks, events, lists, decisions; documents when the Vault lands)
  - *2026-10-06 (Mac checked nightly):* core `Search` (non-AI, local), unit-tested incl. two-device sync. Searches what is already synced on the device; nothing is sent anywhere, stored or indexed (the data is small enough to scan per keystroke). Every word typed must start a word in the item ("den" finds "Dentist", "boil serv" finds "Boiler service"); case, common accents and apostrophes ignored; at least 2 letters. Titles weigh more than places and people, which weigh more than notes; a title holding the whole phrase comes first. Searched: open tasks (title, notes, steps), calendar events (title, place, calendar; upcoming soonest first, then past), Waiting for (what, from whom, notes), decisions incl. replaced ones (statement, why), renewals and bills (title, what it's for, kind, notes), Someday, goals (title, what done looks like), habits, and done tasks (a routine's done occurrences fold into the latest). Groups in a fixed order (Tasks · Calendar · Waiting for · Decisions · Renewals and bills · Someday · Goals · Habits · Done), 20 per group with "and 5 more · keep typing to narrow"; each result has its line ("Planned today 14:00 · ↻ Every weekday", "Tomorrow · 20:00–22:00 · Camp Nou", "Done yesterday", the list row's own line) and a snippet when the match is in the notes, steps or rationale. Results follow edits and sync while the query is set (`MekaCore.search` / `searchView`). Fold: "Search" first in Today's header opens the search pane: an open task opens its detail over the results, a done one unfolds Reopen, a list item opens Lists on its tab with the row unfolded, a goal or habit opens Goals with the row unfolded, events are shown only. Mac: ⌘F (Edit → Search Everything…) or "Search" in Today opens a sheet with the detail beside the results; the same rules.

- [x] Mac database encryption (spike S6); fix the Mac keychain prompts (no Apple-signed cert: use Secure Enclave-wrapped key files)
  - *Slice 1, 2026-10-07 (Mac checked nightly):* the keychain prompts. `SealedKeyFiles` (Mac): the device id, household, enrolment secret, server address and the signing key's enclave handle now live in small files in Application Support/os.meka.mac/keys (folder 0700, files 0600, excluded from Time Machine), each sealed with a P-256 key-agreement key held in the Secure Enclave (its blob only works on this Mac, usable only while it's unlocked): a fresh ephemeral key per write, HKDF-SHA256 bound to the file's name, AES-256-GCM, so a copied, edited or swapped file won't open. Files carry no code-signature ACL, so an ad-hoc build no longer asks for the login keychain password after each rebuild. The first launch moves the old `os.meka.mac.identity.v3` Keychain values across once (all or nothing: if any can't be read, e.g. the prompt was cancelled, nothing is moved and that launch keeps the Keychain, so the device's identity is never lost; old items are left untouched). A Mac without a Secure Enclave keeps the Keychain. Unit-tested (`SealedKeyFilesTests`, with a software key standing in for the enclave). Mac only: the Fold already keeps its keys in the Android Keystore.
  - *Slice 2a, 2026-10-07 (Mac checked nightly):* the SQLCipher linkage (spike S6). The Mac app links Zetetic's official `SQLCipher.swift` package, pinned at 4.19.0 (BSD-style licence, text in docs/third-party-notices.md; free, open source, no service), instead of the system `-lsqlite3`, so MekaKit's SQLiter driver runs on SQLCipher. Without a key SQLCipher reads and writes a plain database exactly like SQLite, so Meka's existing database is untouched and still unkeyed in this slice. `MacDatabase.cipherVersion/opens` and `MacCoreFactory.databaseEncryptionProbe` work on throwaway databases only; `MekaCoreBridgeTests.testDatabaseEngineIsSQLCipher` asserts `PRAGMA cipher_version` is 4.x, that a keyed file has no plain SQLite header, reopens with its key, and is refused with the wrong key or none.

Your data says how the database is protected (Mac: the line above; Fold: "encrypted (SQLCipher, AES-256) with a key Android's Keystore holds"). ADR-002 addendum. - [~] Call assistant for mobile calls at work (Needs Meka #9; code done, waiting on Needs 
  - *Slice 2, 2026-10-08 (core and Mac touched, so Mac checked nightly):* the voice side. **Server** (backend/CallAssistant.kt): a provider-neutral `CallAssistant` flow behind `VoiceProvider` (ADR-009 row) with `TwilioVoice` as the adapter; routes `POST /v1/voice/{provider}/{incoming|recorded|answered|transcribed}`, each refused unless signed by the phone service over the exact public URL and form (`X-Twilio-Signature`; no device or publisher may call them; while the auth token is unset every webhook is refused). The call: if the one switch (`context_mode/work.callAssistant`, read server-side by an indexed latest-op query) is off, or the server has no single household, the call is turned away as busy; otherwise Meka's greeting ("Hi, you've reached Meka's automated assistant. Meka is at work right now and will call you back. Can I take a message, and is it urgent?"), a two-minute recording (beep, # or hang up to finish), then "Is it urgent? Press 1 or say yes…" (keypad or speech, en-GB), then goodbye; nothing recorded → "I didn't hear a message…" and nothing held. The message is written into the synced after-work summary as a server-authored `held_message` of the new kind `VOICE_MESSAGE` (ADR-008 addendum: one new field `urgent`, TrueWins; fixed op ids per call, so retried webhooks write nothing more); the transcript arrives later as its text (not after Done blanked it) and the recording is then deleted from Twilio. Urgent (the answer, or "urgent"/"emergency" in the transcript) → `Push.urgent`: every device woken at once at high FCM priority (still only `{"t":"sync"}`). **Infra:** Secrets Manager `meka-os-dev/voice/twilio` (`{}` until Meka pastes `{"account_sid", "auth_token"}`; read-only grant; about $0.40/month), env `MEKA_VOICE_TWILIO_SECRET`; infra test. **Core:** `CallAssistantScript` (the fixed words), `CallAssistantRules` (held id, caller name incl. withheld/"ANONYMOUS", the urgent answer, transcript tidying, which voice messages alert), `CapturedItem.urgent/isUrgent/displayLine`, summary lines and the nudge count voice messages ("1 voice message · 1 missed call"), and a caller known only by number shows under their listed name on the Fold (ranked as family). **Fold:** an urgent voice message rings through once on "Urgent while at work" ("Voice message · Mum", its transcript or "Left a message with your call assistant and said it's urgent") after the sync the server's wake starts, within an hour of the call; the summary pane shows "Voice message · “…”". **Mac:** the after-work sheet shows the same line. Tests: core CallAssistantTest (both apps, names by number, alerts once, retries, Done), backend CallAssistantTest (the whole call over HTTP, retries, not urgent / no answer / emergency in the words, transcript after Done, switch off / no household / nothing said, signatures, tampering, unset token, recording deletion, high-priority wake), infra test. CI green (run 37702804322; macOS job at the next nightly run; infra and the server changed, so the stack and server redeploy and the phone build is published).
- [~] Gym (Meka, 2026-10-07: getting back into it): MEKA's job is getting you there, not p
  - *Slice 1, 2026-10-08 (core and Mac touched, so Mac checked nightly):* the booking, "Went?" and the rotation. **Core** (core/domain/Sessions.kt, non-AI, pure): `SessionRules.book` books a habit with **Book my sessions** on: from today to Sunday, as many sessions as the week still needs (its target pro rata, less the days ticked), each in the habit's part of the day when there's room (evening 17:00–21:30, morning 06:30–12:00, afternoon 12:00–17:00), else any time 07:00–21:30, clear of timed events (15 min either side to get there and back, an hour before kick-off) and of work hours (15 min after work; bank holidays and weekends free; a night shift keeps its morning), with a rest day between sessions while the week leaves room, and two booked habits never overlapping. Worked out afresh from what's there, so a meeting on the slot moves it and **"Didn't go" or a slot that passed unticked rebooks the remaining sessions** on the days left (never a nag); today's slot is worked out from the whole day, so it stays put and becomes "Did you go?" once over. The **rotation** (No rotation · Push · Pull · Legs · Upper · Lower · Full body A · B) labels sessions in turn from the last one ticked. Today's card: "Today 17:45–18:45" · "Now · until 18:45" · "Did you go? · 17:45–18:45" (Went · Didn't go) · "Went · 2 of 3 this week" with the note and "Next: Thu 17:45 · Pull" · "Not today · no worries" with "Rebooked for Tue 17:45" or "No other slot this week"; Undo. Goals' line "Booked Today 17:45 · Wed 17:45 · Fri 17:45" / "Week done · 3 of 3" / "· no room for 1 more". The planner keeps today's session free and shows it (`DayPlanner.plan(sessions)`); booked habits aren't placed again as flexible ones. Five additive fields (ADR-008 addendum): `habit.bookSlots`, `habit.rotation`, `habit_completion.missed/label/note`. `MekaCore.sessionsView`, `addGym`, `setHabitBooked`, `setHabitRotation`, `sessionWent`, `sessionMissed`, `setSessionNote`, `undoSession`; habits may now be 90 min. Tests: SessionsTest (after work, a meeting and a fixture, bank holidays, ticked days and a met week, did you go, rebooking, a short week, rotation, notes, a habit added late, two habits, night shifts, two devices, the planner), MekaCoreTest (the whole day across two cores), Mac bridge test. **Fold:** Goals → "Add Gym" (3 a week, evenings, an hour, booked) until a booked habit exists; a habit's settings gain "Book my sessions" On/Off and Rotation chips, and its row the booked line in the accent colour; Today shows the session card under Up next (goals/SessionCard.kt; motion catalogue row added). **Mac:** the same: Add Gym, a "Book my sessions" switch and Rotation menu, the line, and the card on Today (Goals/SessionCards.swift) with a note field after Went.   - *Slice 2f, 2026-10-08 (core touched, so Mac checked nightly):* **a block keeps in step with its task**. **Core** (PlanToCalendar.kt, non-AI, pure): `PlanCalendarRules.blockOf` (the latest edit made for the task — its add, a follow-up move or its removal; undone, refused and failed ones don't count — and the event it is now) and `follow`: moving the task (When, Tomorrow from the task or the Needs you stack and its Undo, carrying it over in the shutdown, Plan again) moves its block to the new start keeping its length; Done leaves it; Someday, Skip, Delete or taking its time away removes it; a removed block comes back when the task is planned again with the setting on (or at once, e.g. Undo after Delete, while the removal is still in its five seconds); nothing while a clash waits for Meka's choice. Each step is an ordinary edit with the five-second window, made for the task (`forTask` now also on changes and deletes; no new fields), so Activity lists it ("Keeps a task's block in step with the task") and every view keeps hiding it (`withoutTaskBlocks` also hides the event a follow-up names). An edit for the block still inside its five seconds is taken back and worked out afresh, so Google only gets where the task ended up (moving a task right after Apply re-adds the block at the new time; Delete then Undo sends nothing). Plan again moves an existing block instead of adding a second. Only Meka's own changes on the device he made them on lead to a follow-up (never a sync), so the Fold and the Mac never both send one. Tests: PlanToCalendarTest (moves and Done, removals and coming back, on its way and clash, refused and undone follow-ups), MekaCoreTest (`aTasksBlockFollowsItWhileStillInItsFiveSecondsAndUndoAfterDeleteBringsItBack`). No app code changed (both apps show the core's edit lines and Activity). CI green (run 37801892161; macOS job at the next nightly run; the core was touched, so the server redeploys and GitHub publishes the phone build).
- [~] Edit your calendars from MEKA (Meka, 2026-10-07: "one shop for my life") — right aft
  - *Slice 2g, 2026-10-08 (core touched, so Mac checked nightly):* **a renamed task renames its block, and a block still on its way catches up**. **Core** (PlanToCalendar.kt, non-AI, pure): `PlanCalendarRules.writtenTitle` (the title MEKA last wrote for the task's block: its add or a rename; undone, refused and failed ones don't count) and `follow` now gives `BlockStep.Change` when the task's title (trimmed, "Task" when blank) differs from the block's, only while the block still carries the title MEKA wrote (a block Meka renamed in Google keeps his title, and a move keeps it too); a rename and a move together are one change. `MekaCore.rename` follows like When/Tomorrow do (inside the five seconds the earlier edit is taken back and one change goes). A change made while the block was still on its way to Google (`BlockStep.OnItsWay`, now "The block is still on its way to Google · it follows once it's there") is kept on that device only (`WaitingFollow`, in memory, never synced) and tried again after each sync until the mirror has the block; it's dropped when the task changed again since (that newer change follows by itself, maybe on the other device, so the two never both send) or after 30 minutes. No new fields, no migration, no app code changed. Tests: PlanToCalendarTest (rename, rename and move, Meka's own title kept, undone rename, on its way then caught up, when the wait is dropped), MekaCoreTest (`aRenamedTaskRenamesItsBlockAndABlockStillOnItsWayFollowsAfterTheNextSyncOnThatDeviceOnly`). CI green (run 37803988543, after a test-only fix: the "Added … to Google" line stays two minutes, so the test waits it out; macOS job at the next nightly run; the core was touched, so the server redeploys and GitHub publishes the phone build).
- [~] Edit your calendars from MEKA (Meka, 2026-10-07: "one shop for my life") — right aft
  - *Slice 2h, 2026-10-08 (core touched, so Mac checked nightly):* **a block on its way survives closing the app**. **Core:** `ReplicaStore.localValue/setLocalValue` (device-local values, never synced or pushed; the SQL store keeps them in `replica_meta` under `local:`, apart from the cursor and clock; one new `metaDelete` query, no schema change, no migration; ADR-002 addendum) and `WaitingFollowCodec` (facade, JSON; anything unreadable decodes to nothing, one wait per task). `MekaCore` reads the waits on first use and writes them back whenever they change, so a rename made while the block was on its way follows after the first sync once MEKA is opened again, on that device only. Just after opening nothing has read which accounts allow editing, so the catch-up reads them first; while that fails (offline) the waits stay for the next sync instead of being refused and dropped. The 30-minute limit still applies across the restart. No app code changed. Tests: ReplicaStoreContract (`localValuesPersistApartFromMeta`, in-memory and SQL), WaitingFollowCodecTest, MekaCoreTest (`aBlockStillOnItsWayFollowsAfterTheAppIsClosedAndOpenedAgain`, `aWaitThatOutlivedItsHalfHourIsDroppedAfterOpeningAgain`). - [~] Clean-ups: orphan KMS key, restrict enrolment token after enrolment, ADR-004/005 upd
  - *Slice 1, 2026-10-07:* the deploy gap: the service stack records the commit it was deployed from (`DeployedCommit` output, `-c commit=`), and `deploy.yml` diffs against that instead of `HEAD~1`, so a server commit whose CI failed followed by an app-only fix still deploys (no recorded commit, not an ancestor, or stack unreadable → deploy; infra test added). The enrolment code is narrowed (backend `enrolWithCode`, tested in memory over HTTP and on Postgres): it never brings back a revoked device (403 `revoked`; only the server's own `enrol-device` command can) and can't start a second household (403 `household`); a device that isn't revoked can still reconnect. Both apps show the refusal in words through the core (`Enrolment.refusal`, unit-tested; the Fold and Mac already display `Failed.reason`). ADR-004 and ADR-005 amended (P-256 device keys as built, sealed key files on the Mac, the enrolment rules, the deploy rule, the leftover KMS key). CI green (run 37577176613, after a test-only fix: wire ids are `[a-z0-9]`); deployed, so the stack now records its `DeployedCommit`.
- [~] Clean-ups: orphan KMS key, restrict enrolment token after enrolment, ADR-004/005 upd
  - *Fixed 2026-10-07 (recurred in run 37659606955):* `PostgresOpStore.conn` was `current.get()?.let(block) ?: ds.connection.use(block)`, so a block returning null (finding an op not stored yet) ran again on a second pooled connection while the push's transaction held its own; eight concurrent pushes then starved the pool of eight until Hikari's 30 s timeout. Now it uses the transaction's connection or a fresh one, never both (also halves the queries for every new op the server stores).

- [~] "What MEKA did and why" activity log with undo (lands before any automatic action)
  - *Slice 1, 2026-10-07 (Mac checked nightly):* core `ActivityLog` (non-AI), unit-tested incl. two-device sync, over a new `agent_action` entity (additive, all LWW; ADR-006/008 addenda). What it records today: every notification that actually reached you at Critical, Needs a decision or Heads-up ("Reminded you: Cancel or keep Netflix?" · "Cancel by tomorrow" · "Why: Cancel-by dates · Heads-up"), and every digest that went out ("Sent a digest: Evening digest · 3 things"); one entry per notice however many devices posted it. The undo machinery is in place for the automatic actions to come: `ActivityLog.act` is the one way an automatic action may change Meka's data, recording each field's value before; `undo` puts back only what is still as MEKA left it ("Partly undone: you've changed some of it since"), deletes rather than blanks something MEKA created, and converges when undone on both devices offline. The screen: the last 30 days by day, newest first, "This week: 5 reminders · 2 digests", time, what, the detail, why, and Undo or "Undone at 09:12". Interruption counts stay text-free (ADR-013); the log lives in Meka's own synced data and goes into the export. Fold: "Activity" in Today's header opens the pane; the governor now reports the digest when it reached a live channel. Mac: "Activity" in Today, File → Activity… (⇧⌘A), a sheet; MacNotifier reports the digest by its key (`meka.digest`). CI green (run 76; macOS job at the next nightly run; the core was touched, so the server redeploys).

### "Leaving now" to his wife
- *Slice 1, 2026-10-11 (core + Fold + Mac; core touched, so Mac checked nightly):* **Core** (LeavingNow.kt, non-AI, pure; `LeavingNowTest`, 4): `LeavingRules.notices` — on an office day (`PlacesRules.officeWindow`), a heads-up due at work's end (planned from the morning so the governor wakes for it), stale 90 minutes later; new governor source `NoticeSource.LEAVING` ("Leaving now (a draft to send home)"); its text is the draft itself, word for word what Send sends: "Leaving now, home about 18:40" (leave at work's end or now if later, + the journey home, default 70 min, + TfL's allowance: Thameslink minor +10, major +20 when Great Northern runs ("so I'm coming via King's Cross") else +30; Elizabeth line minor +5, major +15; a stale status adds nothing; rounded up to 5 minutes). One notice per day and line level, all posted at `leaving:<day>` (`postAs`), so a line going bad on the way offers the updated draft once. New `NoticeAction`s SEND_MESSAGE · EDIT_MESSAGE (Fold) and COPY_MESSAGE (Mac), filtered per device by `NotifyRules.actionsOn(n, send)`. `LeavingRules.tap`: Send carries exactly the shown words while they are the draft for leaving up to 10 minutes ago, else `LeavingTap.Changed` with the new notice (nothing sent); Edit skips the check. `waLink` (WhatsApp click-to-chat, 07… → 447…, percent-encoded by hand), `samePerson`/`familyEntry` ("his wife" matches "his wife A…"). Setting `context_mode/leaving_now` (`on`, `to`, `journeyMin`; ADR-008 addendum). **Facade:** `leavingView`, `setLeavingNow`, `leavingTap`; notices through `NoticeSources.collect(leaving)`; `answerSessionNotice` ignores non-session buttons. **Fold:** the governor posts Send / Edit as activity PendingIntents to the new `MessageSendActivity` (shows nothing): Send → `LiveReplies.sendTo` (her live WhatsApp notification's own Reply; `LiveReplies` now remembers a 1:1 notification's person) → a quiet "Sent to his wife" note; otherwise, and for Edit, her chat via click-to-chat with the Family entry's number (else WhatsApp opened with the words copied); a moved-on draft reposts in place. `<queries>` gains com.whatsapp. Work → Leaving now (`LeavingNowSection`: On/Off, To from the Family and always-notify lists, Journey home 50–90 min). **Mac:** Copy on the notification (`NotificationAnswer.body`, NSPasteboard), Work sheet's Leaving now (switch, name field, journey picker). ### Phone updates sometimes fail to install
- *Slice 1 done 2026-10-12 (core + server + Fold + deploy workflow; core touched, so Mac checked nightly):* Core `UpdateFailure` / `UpdateFailureRules` (AppUpdates.kt; `UpdateFailureTest`): the stage (download · check · install), Android's PackageInstaller statuses (the Fold's `UpdateStatusTest` checks they match), `line` (Meka's words, now also for INVALID and TIMEOUT, and "conflicts with" when a conflict isn't about the signature), `detail` ("Android: INSTALL_FAILED_… · STATUS_FAILURE_CONFLICT"), `cleanMessage` (one line, ≤ 300 chars), `storageBand` (never the figure), `isFailure` (ABORTED and the prompt aren't), `retries`/`retryDelayMs` (3 attempts, 2 s then 10 s), `reportLine`, `healthLine`, Activity's summary/why/id; `AppUpdateRules.resumeFrom`/`isWhole`. Health: `DeviceHealth.installedCode`/`updateFailure`; the Updates row says "Build 430 didn't install 06:15 · Android: …" with Try again until that build is in (`HealthTest`). Wire `UpdateFailureCodec` (`UpdateFailureCodecTest`): `POST /v1/releases/failure` (keyed device) and `POST /v1/releases/failures` (newest 10). Facade: `MekaCore.recordUpdateFailure` (Activity "Build 430 didn't install" once, then the report) and `reportUpdateFailure`; `UpdateFailureApi` on `HttpSyncTransport`; `downloadRelease(fromChunk)` / `ReleaseTransfer.download(fromChunk)` and `CHUNK_BYTES` (`UpdateFailureFacadeTest`, `ReleaseTransferTest` +1). Server: `UpdateFailures` + `PostgresUpdateFailureStore` (migration V15 `app_update_failure`, additive, newest 20 kept per household); the publisher may read (not report) failures (`ReleasePublisher.ROUTES`); CLI `publisher-failures <url>` prints the last 14 days as `::warning title=Phone update failed::<time> · build 425 → 430 · install · STATUS_… · <Android's words> · storage … · wifi · 1 attempt` (`UpdateFailuresTest`); deploy.yml's `publish-fold` job runs it after "Anything new for the phone?" (continue-on-error). ADR-013 addendum. Fold: `AppUpdater` rewritten — Install runs in the app's scope (`start`), downloads into `cache/update/meka-<build>.apk`, resumes from its whole chunks and retries 3 times with pauses, reuses a whole kept file whose hash matches (Try again), then copies it into Android's session; `onStatus` keeps `EXTRA_STATUS_MESSAGE`; ABORTED → Ready; a prompt that comes while locked or off screen waits for MEKA's next open (MainActivity.onStart); a failure shows Android's words under the card's line (fades in), goes to Activity and Health (kept in prefs across restarts) and is reported (again on the next check if offline); old kept downloads are cleared. Mac: `DeviceHealth`'s two new arguments (nil). Gradle can't run in the build container, so CI is the compile check for the facade, server and Fold. Commits d7a7dd5 + c99588b (a smart cast across modules in `PostgresUpdateFailureStore`), CI run 425 (38209575883) green.

- *Slice 2 (2026-10-13, "Session files in use" from Meka's Fold):* core `InstallSessionRules` (AppUpdates.kt): `toAbandon` (every own session except a live outstanding one: committed < 10 min ago and still listed by Android), `onTap` (START · SHOW_PROMPT · WAIT), `apkName` ("meka-<code>-<ms>.apk"), `retriesItself` (only STATUS_FAILURE/an exception saying "Session files in use", once per tap), and `UpdateFailureRules.line` saying "Android was still holding an earlier install…". Fold `AppUpdater`: a process-wide install Mutex (companion), `abandonOwnSessions()` before `createSession`, the session id and commit time kept, a tap while Android has the install re-shows its prompt, the auto-retry from the status receiver and from a thrown write (1.5 s pause, kept download reused), and `check()` releasing a Confirming card whose session went quiet. Tests: core `InstallSessionTest` (7).

- *Slice 3 (2026-10-13, the root cause of "Session files in use"):* the 11:12 report (deploy run 525's `publish-fold`: build 942 → 973, `INSTALL_FAILED_INTERNAL_ERROR: Session files in use`, STATUS_FAILURE) came from build 942, which already had slice 2 (one install at a time, stale sessions abandoned, unique names, one fresh retry), so stale sessions weren't the cause. Android checks at commit that every file written into the session has been let go, and the app's close of the write stream reaches the system asynchronously (a revocable fd / file bridge), so committing straight after `openWrite(...).use { }` raced it; a fresh session committed just as fast raced it again, and a later manual go won the race (the Fold restarted on 973 at 11:12). Core `InstallSessionRules` (AppUpdates.kt): `AUTO_RETRIES` 1 → 3, `SETTLE_MS` 1 s, 2.5 s, 5 s, 8 s and `settleMs(retriesSoFar)`, `handsToAndroidsInstaller` (files in use after the fresh sessions; exactly one of retry or hand over for every count), `reportMessage` ("… · 4 sessions tried · handed to Android's installer"). Fold `AppUpdater`: `commit` waits `settleMs` between closing the write and `session.commit`; once the fresh sessions are used up, `handToAndroidsInstaller` abandons its sessions and hands the kept, hash-checked APK to Android's own installer (ACTION_VIEW through a new FileProvider `${applicationId}.updates` over `cache/update/` only, `res/xml/update_paths.xml`), shown now or when Navilife is next open and unlocked (the same `pendingPrompt` path), and reports it to the server only (not Activity or Health); a real failure's report carries the sessions tried. Tests: InstallSessionTest (fresh sessions, longer settles, the hand-over, the report line).

### A morning brief worth listening to

- *Slice 1, 2026-10-12 (core + both apps through the core; core and macos touched, so Mac checked nightly):* the spoken brief rewritten as a chief-of-staff briefing in natural sentences (non-AI, pure, `BriefScript.kt`). `MorningBriefView.story` (`BriefStory`, additive, nothing synced) carries what the script needs beyond the pane: the epoch day, weekend, office day, work's end, both places' weather, TfL's route line (spoken), today's timed events (`BriefEvent`), the focus (`BriefFocus`, title + why) and the smaller ones counted, Needs you decisions (conflicts, call credit), today's habits by name with the week so far, the week's goals line, home and family (Today's bins, date night, gifts, trip spoken lines) and one open week goal. `MorningBrief.view` fills the events, focus (`BriefScriptRules.focus`: overdue → due today → moves one of this week's goals → Up next; at most 3, the weekend 1; repeating chores last in their kind), habits (`BriefScriptRules.habits`: due or behind, not done today: "gym, 1 of 3 this week", "reading, a 12-day streak") and goals; the facade adds office, places, route, Needs you and family. `BriefScriptRules.script`: greeting → "It's Monday 12 October, an office day, finishing at half past 5" (weekend "no work today"; a holiday or leave as its line) → trains and both places on an office day, else the weather → the calendar (all-day things, "First up, Standup at half past 9", the next two, the shape: busy morning / clear morning / full day / "Free after …", the first clash) → focus ("Three things to focus on. First, Renew passport, it's overdue. Then … And …, it moves your goal, Q4 plan. Plus 3 smaller ones.") → Needs you, chases, lists (weekday) → habits, week's goals (weekday), fasting → school and family → 3 headlines (Barça first as listed) → the one-liner (31 lines, some about his focus, goal, habit, office or weekend; picked by epoch day so none repeats within 30 days and both devices say the same) → "Say “plan my day” or “more news”". ### Messages grouped per chat, and Mark read in WhatsApp
- [x] **Messages grouped per chat, and Mark read in WhatsApp (Meka, 2026-10-12 07:44: one WhatsApp group gave him ~20 separate items to open; asked whether MEKA can mark them read in WhatsApp).** (1) **One card per conversation**: everything new from the same chat (group or person, WhatsApp or SMS) since he last looked becomes one card — chat name, "20 new · 4 people", a 1–3 line summary of what matters (AI from the messages only; deterministic fallback = last 3 messages), anything addressed to him or with a question/date/request pulled to the top, and Expand to read all in order. (2) **Mark read**: WhatsApp's own notification carries a "Mark as read" action (Notification.Action with SEMANTIC_ACTION_MARK_AS_READ); while that notification is still in the shade MEKA can fire that action on Meka's tap — official Android API, no unofficial library. Card button "Mark read in WhatsApp" (and on Expand → Done, a setting "Mark read when I finish a card", off by default because it sends blue ticks if read receipts are on). (3) **Clear the notification once consumed** (Meka, 08:47): when Meka finishes a card (Done, Mark read, or reads it to the end in Expand), MEKA clears that chat's WhatsApp/SMS notifications from the shade with NotificationListenerService.cancelNotification(key) — **after** firing Mark read if that was chosen (the action disappears with the notification) — and clears MEKA's own notification for the card. Clearing hides a notification only; it never marks read on its own and never deletes anything in WhatsApp. Never sends anything else. ## Trading approvals from Kestrel
- *Slice 1, 2026-10-12 (server + infra only; no core or app change, the apps already show approvals):* the approval desk. **Server** (`backend/ApprovalDesk.kt`): `ApprovalAsker` (id, label, allowed kinds, public key source) and `ApprovalDesk.kestrel` ("Kestrel", trades only). `POST /v1/approvals/request` ({ref, kind, title, lines, expiresAtMs}) writes an `approval` entity once as server ops (id `ApprovalRules.entityId("Kestrel", ref)`, so a retry is the same card and writes nothing), source fixed by the server, fields cleaned by `ApprovalRules.requestFields`, 429 past 10 waiting, wakes the devices; `POST /v1/approvals/status` ({ref}) answers state, asked/expires and, once answered, decidedAtMs, confirmedBy and decisionKey (404 for an unknown ref). Auth: `Authorization: Asker kestrel` + the MEKA1 signature (same `RequestVerifier` as devices and the release publisher); an unknown name, another key, a replayed nonce or a signature for the other path is 401, no key set is 403, and every route that takes a device answers 403 to an asker. `approvalsFromEnv` (`MEKA_APPROVALS_KESTREL_SECRET`, read with `SecretsManagerPublisherKey`). **Infra:** secret `meka-os-dev/approvals/kestrel` (`{}`), env var, read-only grant (+ stack test). **Docs:** docs/kestrel-integration.md (keys, signing, both routes, polling, the rules: no credential ever in MEKA, no answer = no trade, act once per decisionKey; slice 2's coming fields), ADR-006 addendum. Tests: backend `ApprovalDeskTest` (6). Needs Meka #27 for Kestrel's side.
- *Slice 2, 2026-10-12 (core + server + Fold + Mac; core and macos touched, so Mac checked nightly; the Swift was written without a Mac to compile on):* **a yes is signed by Meka's finger.** **Core** (Approvals.kt): `ApprovalRules.answerMessage` (MEKA-APPROVAL1, id, "approved", kind, source, decisionKey, decidedAtMs, expiresAtMs, device, SHA-256 of the title and lines; `Sha256` moved to core/sync so the rules can hash), `prepare` → `ApprovalPrep` (the text to sign, its key and time, or the refusal shown before any prompt), `decide(signature, decidedAtMs)` (a yes needs a signature and a prep under 5 minutes old, else `NEEDS_BIOMETRIC` / new `STALE`; writes `answerSignature`, `answerPublicKey`), `ApprovalKeys` over a new `approval_key` entity (id = device, written by that device; ADR-008 addendum). Facade: `prepareApproval`, `approve(approvalId, decisionKey, decidedAtMs, publicKeyBase64, signatureBase64, keyLabel)` (replaces `approve(confirmedWithBiometric)`), `registerApprovalKey`. **Server** (`ApprovalDesk`): status adds `title`, `lines` and, only when every answer field came from the answering device, that device registered the same key itself and the ECDSA signature verifies, `answerSignature`, `answerDevice`, `answerPublicKey`, `answerMessage`; new asker route `POST /v1/approvals/keys` (each device's own key, for Kestrel to pin). **Fold:** `FoldApprovalKey` (Keystore P-256, StrongBox when there, `setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG)`, invalidated by a new fingerprint; renewed and re-registered with "Fingerprints changed on this phone · approval key renewed · approve again"), `FoldBiometric.sign` (BiometricPrompt with the key's CryptoObject), Approve in `ApprovalCardView` prepares → signs → approves; the key is registered at process start when a fingerprint is enrolled. **Mac:** `MacApprovalKey` (Secure Enclave, `.privateKeyUsage` + `.biometryCurrentSet`, handle kept by `DeviceIdentity.approvalKey`), `MacBiometric.sign` (Touch ID, then the key signs with that LAContext), `CoreModel.approve`/`finishApprove` pass only Strings and an Int64 back to the core; registered at start. **Docs:** docs/kestrel-integration.md (the signed text, the keys route, pinning, Kestrel's five checks), ADR-006 and ADR-008 addenda. Tests: ApprovalsTest +2 (the text, its hash against FIPS 180-4's "abc", keys), ApprovalsFacadeTest (prep, stale, the signed yes and the key reaching the server), backend ApprovalDeskTest +1 and extended (a real P-256 signature verifies; no key, a key registered by another device, a wrong text, answer fields written by another device and a decline all carry no signature; the keys route), bridge `testApprovalsReachSwift` extended.

## Today's watch face: smaller on the cover screen, and it shrinks as you scroll (Meka, 2026-10-12 18:04)

- *Slice 1, 2026-10-13 (core + Fold + Mac; Mac checked nightly):* (1), (2b) and the second hand (07:01). The code put the closed Fold's face at 96 dp (`DayRingHeader.COMPACT_DP`, not the board's guessed 168), so "about a fifth smaller" is **78 dp** (`WatchFaceRules.COVER_DP`, `headerDp(cover)`; the open Fold and the Mac keep 150). New core `WatchFaceLook` (WatchFace.kt; the Day ring keeps `DayRingLook`): the bezel 1.75 dp at the 150 dp face (58 % of the old 3 dp track, which with the 1.5 dp breathing edge read as the thick outline), scaled with the face (min 0.6 dp), placed a quarter-dp outside the arcs and clear of the week's goal ring; it draws round from 12 at 80 % on the opening, then breathes (`bezelAlpha(glow, shown)` blends from 80 % so it never blinks); a 0.5 dp hairline at 35 % just inside it; the arcs' own faint 1 dp track (20 %); the glow half the Day ring's (4 dp, 11 % peak, 4 layers); the shimmer at 1.4 × the bezel. The second hand: a 1 dp needle (scaled, min 0.6) from 18 % of the radius behind the centre to the markers' outer ends, three halo layers under it (3.5 ×/2.4 ×/1.6 × the needle at 12 %/21 %/35 %), the cap (2.6 dp scaled) drawn last over all three hands; no comet tail. Fold `WatchFaceDial` (Today, the bedside clock and screen saver) and `TodayRoute` (`headerDp`); Mac `WatchFaceView`/`WatchFaceLiveLayer`. No widget draws the face. Tests: `WatchFaceLookTest` (6), `TodayHeaderRingTest` (cover width), bridge `testWatchFaceLookReachesSwift`. Motion catalogue's Watch face row updated.

## Inbox autopilot — email (Meka, 2026-10-12 21:01)

*The board entry as it stood when the item was done (2026-10-14):*

- [x] **Inbox autopilot — email, take after the Ask polish (Meka, 2026-10-12 21:01: "what I struggle with is keeping a clean inbox… it builds up, then I spend hours cleaning it, then it happens again").** Decided: (a) MEKA may **read, organise (archive, label, link) and send only on his tap**; (b) junk reviewed and useless mail deleted (= moved to Trash, recoverable 30 days — **never permanent delete**), newsletters and receipts **auto-archived but shown to him**, unsubscribe done for him; (c) **three accounts**: personal Gmail, personal Outlook/Hotmail, and a **business Gmail for his side hustle**. Builds on ADR-005 (email) and the policy engine; every automatic action is logged in Activity with Undo and has an off switch in What MEKA may do → Email. Slices: (1) **Connect mail** on both apps: Google (gmail.modify + gmail.send) and Microsoft (Mail.ReadWrite + Mail.Send) consent per account, tokens server-side like calendars; an account label (Personal · Business · Outlook); Setup row + Needs Meka steps (the Google app stays unverified-for-personal-use, which these scopes allow for the owner; publishing to Production per #17 removes the 7-day expiry). Incremental sync (Gmail history id / Graph delta), last 60 days on first connect. (2) **Sorting** each new email (rules first — List-Unsubscribe/List-Id, Gmail categories, known receipt/shipping senders, his contacts — AI only for the unclear ones, words only): Needs you · FYI · Newsletter · Receipt/order · Notification · Promo · Junk. (3) **Autopilot actions**: Newsletters → archived + label MEKA/Newsletters; Receipts/orders → archived + MEKA/Receipts, amount/merchant/return-by extracted (feeds money, returns, deliveries); Notifications/Promos → archived; Junk folder reviewed daily: obvious spam/scams → Trash, anything legit-looking in Junk rescued to the inbox and flagged; nothing from contacts, his wife, the school, the bank/HMRC/employer domains or threads he replied to is ever auto-archived or trashed. (4) **"Archived for you" card** twice a day (12:30 and 18:30 with the digests): "14 tidied · 3 receipts £84.20 · 9 newsletters · 2 to Trash" with each line expandable to read, Put back, or Unsubscribe. (5) **Unsubscribe for him**: per sender Unsubscribe (RFC 8058 one-click POST, else List-Unsubscribe mailto sent from that account, else open the link), and a weekly "Not opened in 30 days · unsubscribe from 11?" with one tap for all; unsubscribed senders' future mail goes straight to Trash; all logged. (6) **Needs-you cards**: the inbox holds only what needs him; each is a card with a summary, linked thread/related emails (same thread, same order number, same person+topic), and actions Reply (AI draft in his tone, sent from the same account only on tap), Done (archive), Snooze (until a time/date), Task, Waiting for (chase drafted after N days). Business account mail shows in its own section with a Business chip; replies always go from the account it came to. (7) **Ten-minute inbox**: a daily Inbox moment (morning or evening, his choice) — "6 need you · 2 min each" — swipe through cards (Reply/Done/Snooze/Task); the goal line "Inbox clear 4 days running". (8) **Backlog clean-up, once per account**: scan the existing inbox, group by sender/category, show a plan ("Archive 3,412 newsletters/promos older than 30 days · Trash 640 junk · keep 212 that may need you") and apply only after he taps Approve (big batch = approval, then Undo for 30 days). (9) Brief, week ahead, Ask/Talk ("anything important in my email?", "what did the school say?") read from the sorted mail. Tests per slice: classification rules (never-touch list, receipts, newsletters), action planner, unsubscribe method choice, Undo; nothing sends without a tap.

Pure readers `GmailHistory`, `GraphDelta`, `MailAddress`. **Store** (`MailStore`, `InMemoryMailStore`, `PostgresMailStore`; migration **V20** `mail_message` (headers, `headers_at` NULL while pending) + `mail_sync` (cursor), additive): `Integrations.syncMail` now runs `syncHeaders` after the inbox check: changes since the cursor (expired → forget and list again), up to `HEADERS_PER_CHECK` = 300 pending headers read, then anything received over `MAIL_WINDOW_MS` (60 days) ago dropped; Disconnect forgets the account's rows and cursor. Server: `GoogleSpeech` (Cloud Text-to-Speech `v1/voices` and `v1/text:synthesize`, MP3, key in `X-Goog-Api-Key`, 5 s for a clip), key from `meka-os-dev/speech/google` else `meka-os-dev/maps/google`, cached a minute; `SpeechService` lists Google's voices first (British, then American; Aoede, Kore, Leda, Charon, Puck, Orus first), Polly's first voice stays the default; a chosen Google voice speaks on its own meter (`speech_usage_google`, V26, additive) up to 900k a month, else (or on failure/timeout) the same words once in the default Polly voice, `googleFailedAtMs` kept; Polly's cap counts only Polly. Research: the CMA's interim retailer JSON feeds were withdrawn on 1 May 2026; the statutory **Fuel Finder** scheme (DESNZ) publishes every UK forecourt's prices (within 30 min of a change) through a REST API with OAuth client credentials from a free developer account (GOV.UK One Login): `https://www.fuel-finder.service.gov.uk/api/v1`, `POST /oauth/generate_access_token` `{client_id, client_secret}`, `GET /pfs?batch-number=N` (forecourts, 500 a batch: `node_id`, `trading_name`, `brand_name`, closures, `location{latitude, longitude, postcode}`) and `GET /pfs/fuel-prices?batch-number=N` (`fuel_prices[{fuel_type, price, price_last_updated, price_change_effective_timestamp}]`), read from an open-source client's source; the exact fuel-type codes aren't documented there, so they are read leniently (E10, E5, B7/B7_STANDARD/diesel, B7_PREMIUM/SDV). **Core** (FuelPrices.kt, non-AI, pure; `FuelPricesTest` 5): `FuelKind` (E10 default, E5, B7, SDV); `CarFields.FUEL` per car (additive, LWW; `Car.setFuel`, `CarEntry.fuel`, `CarView.fuel`; ADR-008 addendum); `FuelRules.kindOf`/`pence` (pounds → pence, 50p–£4 else dropped), `nearest` (the cheapest 5 within 8 km, nearer first on a tie), `block` ("UNLEADED (E10)" or "DIESEL · THE GOLF", "Cheapest within 8 km · Tesco 139.9p · 2.2 km", rows "139.9p" · "2.2 km · AB1 2CD · updated today 13:00", stale after 3 days "price from …", the saving "A 50-litre fill there is £3.00 less than at Shell (1.1 km)" when ≥ £1), `fuelsFor` (a block per fuel the live cars take), `view` and its states (off, loading, failed, no location, offline), `mapsUrl`. **Wire** FuelCodec (`POST /v1/car/fuel`: a two-decimal point, refused finer, and a known fuel; ≤ 10 stations; `FuelCodecTest` 2). **Facade**: `FuelApi` on the HTTP transport (404 → off), `fuelNearby(lat, lon)` (rounded first, one ask per fuel, never throws), `setCarFuel`. **Server** (integrations/FuelFinder.kt): the keys from `meka-os-dev/car/fuelfinder` (cached a minute; `{}` = "off"), an in-memory copy of forecourts (a day) and prices (an hour), refreshed in the background only when a phone asks and the copy is stale (the very first ask says "loading"; a failed fetch is retried after 10 min; the old copy keeps answering); closed forecourts and ones outside the UK box left out; the point is neither stored nor logged and never sent on. `FuelFinderTest` (5, a recorded-shape sample, invented forecourts). **Infra**: the secret (`{}`), `MEKA_CAR_FUEL_SECRET`, read-only grant; infra test. **Fold**: the Car pane's FUEL NEARBY (one coarse fix when the pane opens via `HereLocation.locate`, Allow asks for approximate location, Look again; a block per fuel with the forecourts, the cheapest in brass, a tap opens directions in his maps app; each car's "takes unleaded (E10) · Change" with the four fuels). Help entry tip and keywords (docs/help/car.md), motion catalogue row. Needs Meka #34 (the free Fuel Finder developer keys).

## Barça match day (Meka approved 2026-10-12)

- **Slice 1 (2026-10-15): kick-off in UK time, where to watch it, and a heads-up an hour before** (core + server; both apps show it through the governor and the event's notes; Mac checked nightly; no migration, nothing new stored). **Server** (integrations/TvListings.kt): `UkTvListings` reads the public listings page live-footballontv.com/barcelona-on-tv.html (a plain GET, no key, nothing about the household sent; at most every 6 h, a failed read keeps the last good page): HTML to lines (block tags break, inline tags don't, script/style dropped), date headings ("Tuesday 20th October 2026"), then per match time / "Home v Away" / competition / channel lines; a channel line must start like a known UK broadcaster (TNT Sports, Amazon Prime Video, Premier Sports, LaLigaTV, Disney+, HBO Max, Sky Sports…, run-together pills split), so a footer is never a channel. `EspnTeamFixtures(tv)` writes each match's notes: "Kick-off 20:00 UK time" (Europe/London) and "On UK TV: TNT Sports 2 · HBO Max" (matched by UK date, nearest kick-off), "… · channel to be confirmed", "Not on UK TV, per the listings" (only when the page read and lists a later day) or "UK TV not listed yet". Application wires `EspnTeamFixtures(UkTvListings())`. TvListingsTest (5, invented page). **Core** (BarcaMatch.kt): `BarcaMatchRules.isMatch` (Fixtures feed, timed, not "(kick-off TBC)"), `kickOffLine`, `watchLine`, `notices`: `NoticeSource.BARCA` "Barça match day" (heads-up, adjustable in Notifications on both apps), "PSG v Barça · 20:00" · "Champions League · kick-off in an hour · on TNT Sports 2 · HBO Max", at kick-off − 60 min, standing 15 min after, CLOCK precision, keyed on the kick-off (a moved match gets a fresh one), nothing for a hidden match or a hidden Fixtures calendar; quiet hours through the governor; `NoticeSources.collect` adds it beside weekend football. - **Slice 2 (2026-10-15): the live score, each goal and full time** (core + server; both apps show it through the governor, the event's notes and News; Mac checked nightly; no migration, nothing new stored). **Server** (integrations/Fixtures.kt): `EspnTeamFixtures` remembers each match its schedules list (league and kick-off, in memory) and, with the wall clock (production constructor), reads ESPN's public scoreboard `…/soccer/<league>/scoreboard?dates=yyyyMMdd` (no key, nothing about the household) for each match from 10 min before kick-off to 24 h after; `parseScores` takes Barça's event (team id 83): state pre/in/post, both scores (string or object), the clock ("67'", "half time"), "after extra time"/"after penalties", and the scoring plays (not shootouts) as "23' Lewandowski (Barça)" ("F. de Jong" → "de Jong", " og", " pen"). `LiveScore.lines` writes "Live: Barça 2–1 Getafe · 67'" / "Full time: …" and "Goals: …" ahead of the kick-off/TV lines; a final score is read once and kept; a match the schedule drops after kick-off stays in the window with its result; a scoreboard that can't be read says "Live score unavailable" only within 150 min of kick-off. ## Mac sidebar rows can't be clicked (Fix first, 2026-10-15)

### Slices
- Slice 1 (2026-10-15): ShellView's sidebar `List(selection:)` was bound to a computed `Binding` whose setter called `model.go(to:)`; on Meka's macOS 27 clicks never switched screens. Now a `@State sidebarPick` drives the List, `.onChange(of: sidebarPick)` calls `go`, and `.onChange(of: model.destination, initial: true)` keeps the highlight in step with ⌘1–⌘8, the command bar and search. Each row is full-width with `.contentShape(Rectangle())` and a `simultaneousGesture(TapGesture)` that switches directly (both paths go through `ShellNav.sidebarPick`, so the second is a no-op). Clicks log to OSLog (category `shell`). `ShellNav.sidebarRows` / `sidebarPick` added; ShellNavTests +1 (every row switches from every screen). Overlays checked: the ⌘K overlay is only present while open and EventUndoBar is empty unless an undo is offered, so neither covers the sidebar. Mac checked nightly.

The Mac's type scale in the macOS idiom and View → Text Size. `design/tokens/tokens.json` gains `macSize` on every type token except the clock (greeting 26, upNextTitle 20, nowTitle 17, itemTitle 15, body 13, itemMeta/metaStrong 12, sectionLabel/caption/captionStrong 11, micro 10); `design/generate.mjs` emits the Swift tokens as computed `static var`s reading `MekaTextScale.shared.factor` (an `@Observable` class in MekaTokens.swift, so every view body that reads a token redraws when it changes; sizes rounded to the half point, tracking scaled with it). ## Take first: the inbox still looks untouched — slice 1 (2026-10-15)

**New mail tidied in every account, and marked read.** Diagnosis from the code (no server access from a build run): `syncHeaders` read up to 300 headers a check one call each and any non-401 failure (`Http.call` throws on 429/5xx and `WriteRefused` on 403, which is how Gmail reports per-user rate limits) aborted the whole check, so sorting, Autopilot and the cards never ran and the account showed "Couldn't reach it last time"; and `pending` was oldest-listed first, so a new email's headers waited behind the first 60-day listing (thousands of ids). Outlook's Graph delta carries no labels or list headers, so `MailSortRules.sort` could only call unknown senders a person (unsure, needs you) and nothing was tidy-kind there.
Server: header reads newest-listed first (`MailStore.pending`, both stores) and a refusal `break`s the loop (ReconnectRequired still ends the check); the backlog's header reads only when no live header is pending. `bulkLook` (Outlook only): up to `BULK_LOOKS_PER_CHECK` = 40 of the newest emails the rules can only call a person's (`MailSortRules.wantsHeaderLook`) get `MailProvider.bulkHeaders` (Graph `internetMessageHeaders`) once a process (cached, re-applied if the feed brings the bare headers back); one with List-Unsubscribe/List-Id/bulk is stored with them and re-sorted. Gmail's metadata read adds Precedence and Auto-Submitted; bulk ones carry the server-only label `NAVILIFE_BULK` (`MailSortReason.BULK`, notification, sure; after list rules, never over public bodies or banks). `MailProvider.markRead` (Gmail batchModify UNREAD, Outlook PATCH isRead): Autopilot and the Junk review mark the unread ones they moved read, the backlog clean-up what it moved; Undo (tidies and the clean-up) marks put-back mail unread; all only while `MailAutopilotSetting.markRead` (field `markRead` on the `mail_autopilot` context_mode entity, absent = on). `MailTidy.marksRead` (not KEEP/RESCUE). Account line "Connected · checked N ago" (no "sorted, nothing moved yet").
Tests: MailSortTest (bulk, wantsHeaderLook, line), MailTidyTest (markRead), MailSyncTest (refused read doesn't fail the check and new mail first, Gmail bulk header, mark read/undo/off, Outlook header look and tidy, Outlook refusal carries on). No migration. Mac test bridge updated (MailAutopilotSetting's new parameter); Mac checked nightly.

## Take first: the inbox still looks untouched — slice 2 (2026-10-15)

**The backlog clean-up comes to Needs you, at a week, with a fresh plan.** Core: `MailBacklogRules.ARCHIVE_AFTER_DAYS` 30 → 7 (newsletters, promos, notifications and receipts; junk any age as before); `PLAN_VERSION` = 2 written by the server as `planVersion` on the `mail_backlog` entity (absent = 1; ADR-008 addendum, additive field, no migration) and `readyAtMs` now written as 0 while scanning; `needsReplan(b)` = an older version, not approved, nothing applied. `MailBacklogRules.cards(backlogs, paused)`: one `DecisionCard` per account (newest plan) that `canApprove`, kind `MAIL_CLEANUP`, "Clean up Personal" · "Archive 2,140 newsletters and promos older than a week · Trash 310 junk · keep 212 that may need you · nothing moves until you approve", → Approve (`DecisionEffect.APPROVE_BACKLOG`, the same synced approval as Mail's), ← Later (set aside), ↑ Review (`DecisionEffect.OPEN_MAIL`); none while paused. `NeedsYouStackRules.build(mail = …)` puts them after the tasks, before the lists card; the facade passes them in.

## Group chats show as one group, not one card per sender (Take first, Meka 2026-10-15 20:28)

Done 2026-10-16 in one slice. Core: `AfterWorkSummaries.build` groups by card key — a group chat's messages by `app + People.key(ChatTitleRules.clean(conversation))`, everything else by person as before; `groupCard` makes the group's card (title = the group's newest cleaned name, `senders` most recent first, counts without the notices, `latestText` "Sender: words", family when the group is on the family list or every sender is family). New `GroupChatRules` (MENTIONED, isMention/isMentionText — WhatsApp's "Mentioned you" notice as sender or whole text, groupOf, senders, sendersLine). `PersonSummary` gains `conversation`, `senders`, `mentioned`, `isGroup`, `cardKey` (group and person never share a key), `shownItems` (without the notices), `itemLabel(item)`; `line` leads with the senders on a group's card; `keeping` recounts a group and drops it when only its notice is left; `blockNumber` null for groups. A notice with no group goes to the group it names, else the group whose messages are within 10 minutes, else is dropped. Ranking: urgent, family, mentioned groups, then latest. `AfterWorkSummary.groupKeys` (the digest's group keys); headline "N chats" once any card is a group; `itemCount` counts shown items. `HeldPreviewRules.build` names the sender for a group's items ("Sam · Home"). Fold: WorkScreens keys cards by `cardKey`, the Mentioned you chip, each opened group line under its sender's name; NeedsYouRoute passes the after-work groups to the group digest's `inChats` so a group is never shown twice. Mac: AfterWorkSheet keyed by `cardKey`, the chip, sender labels. Tests: GroupChatCardsTest (three senders → one card; 1:1 unchanged and keyed apart; bundled title same group; mention folds in and ranks first, loose notice matched by time or dropped; recount after Done; groupKeys match the digest; family group and held preview); AfterWorkTest and HeldMessagesTest updated for the group card. No migration.

The item as it stood:

- [ ] **Take first: group chats show as one group, not one card per sender (Meka, 20:28: "messages from the same group I created yesterday show as different messages: the ones from Alex, Sam and Jordan").** AfterWorkSummaries.build groups by `personKey`, so "Oakfield testing" splits into Alex Lane, Sam, Jordan Lee (and another group the same way). (1) Group by **conversation** when the item has one (key = app + conversation), title = the group name, a line "Alex, Sam and Jordan · 9 messages", the latest line prefixed with the sender ("Alex: Some more feedback to follow"); expanded shows every message with sender and time. One-to-one chats stay per person. (2) WhatsApp's **"Mentioned you"** summary notification is not a person: fold it into its group as a "Mentioned you" chip on that group card (and sort that group first among non-family), never its own card. (3) A group is never shown twice: if the evening digest already holds that group, the after-work summary links to it instead of duplicating (or the digest skips groups the after-work summary has). (4) People counts count senders and groups sensibly ("6 chats · 34 messages"). (5) Mac parity. Tests: three senders in one group → one card; mention folds in; 1:1 unchanged.
